name: Liberal Kemalism
summary: Liberal Kemalism reads Atatürk's republican revolution through liberal commitments: secular republicanism and a civic Turkish nation, combined with individual freedoms, multi-party democracy, private enterprise over etatism, and equal rights for women. Its best-known formulator Ahmet Ağaoğlu criticized the Republican People's Party's one-party authoritarianism while still sharing the Kemalist belief in modernizing society from above.
scope: The strand of Kemalism associated with Ahmet Ağaoğlu and the 1930 Free (Liberal) Republican Party of Fethi Okyar, built from the 1924 constitution, Ağaoğlu's writings as described by scholars, and the party's reported programme. Answers are for a committed modern adherent of that strand; it excludes the statist and military-guardian mainstream of Kemalism and later conservative-liberal Turkish parties. Many answers are inferred because few sources record this strand's positions in detail.

sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Six principles, laicism, populism against class conflict, republicanism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Free Republican Party favoured private enterprise over state enterprise and an end to monopolies, but Ağaoğlu disliked Anglo-Saxon laissez-faire, so the agreement is moderate.

public-ownership.rationale: The liberal wing opposed etatist state enterprise and wanted private initiative, so broad public ownership of industry is not its line.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources give no tax-progressivity stance; the party sought lower taxes overall while Ağaoğlu backed welfare spending, so this is a genuine split.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1924 constitution lists property among natural rights but allows expropriation for public interest with prior compensation, so it is a strong but not absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Atatürk's quoted view was that markets should not be intervened in without necessity but none is wholly free, which leaves regulation level unresolved.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses drug policy; a modernizing, order-minded Kemalist outlook leans against full legalization, though liberals may differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The constitution limits liberty only where others' rights are affected, which could cut either way for hate speech; no direct source.

strong-leader.rationale: Ağaoğlu condemned the CHP's one-party authoritarianism after 1926 and argued for multi-party politics, so bypassing gridlock via a strong leader is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberal Kemalism is a state-founding republican creed with a vigorous state reforming society; anarchist rejection of the state is far outside it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: Liberal Kemalists criticized authoritarian abuse yet venerate the republic's military heritage; adherents are split with no stated position.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

traditional-family.rationale: Ağaoğlu pushed gender equality and women's independence and wanted secular morality rather than tradition, though he valued the family for social ends.

more-religion-public.rationale: Laicism is a core principle: keep religion out of government, curb the clerical establishment and subordinate religion to the state.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ağaoğlu helped found the Turkish Hearths and held that the Turkish nation must be built on its historical and cultural origins.

gradual-change.rationale: Kemalism is reformist and Jacobin, imposing rapid change from above against established religious institutions, and Ağaoğlu shared its top-down modernization.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Free Republican Party sought closer ties to the League of Nations, but sovereignty was held to rest unrestrictedly with the nation, so views conflict.

free-trade.rationale: The party's programme favoured openness to foreign capital and fewer monopolies, supporting freer trade though not as doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Atatürk's maxim was peace at home and abroad, balancing national interest with cooperation; adherents split on the framing.

central-planning.rationale: The Free Republican Party rejected statist economics and constant state intervention in favour of private enterprise.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Ağaoğlu opposed inherited privilege and favoured meritocracy, yet the party defended private property; no stated tax position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of investment is the etatism that the liberal wing opposed in favour of private enterprise.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A private-enterprise, anti-collectivist programme rejects abolition of money and wage labour.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Kemalist populism rejected class conflict and favoured national unity, which has a corporatist flavour, but the liberal strand opposed state-run bodies; split leaning against.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized one-party abuses in a 1926 report to Atatürk and wrote the programme for an opposition party seeking multi-party democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Republicanism is a founding principle; the monarchy and caliphate were abolished and replaced by elected officials.

democracy-best.rationale: The Free Republican Party aimed at multi-party democracy, though Ağaoğlu saw liberties as educative, so support is firm but qualified.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1924 constitution made the Assembly the sole representative of the nation; referendums were not part of the tradition.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the base of power is a socialist model rejected by a republican, parliamentary, anti-class-conflict tradition.

right-to-secede.rationale: Kemalism builds a unitary indivisible nation-state whose single Turkish political identity covers all citizens.

natural-rulers.rationale: Ağaoğlu stressed meritocracy over inherited privilege and the 1924 constitution abolished group and family privileges.

political-violence-never.rationale: The republic was founded through a war and revolution while liberals oppose repression; no firm position.

war-builds-character.rationale: Atatürk's foreign policy stressed peace at home and in the world, so glorifying war is inconsistent.

separate-church-state.rationale: Laicism keeps religion out of government, though in practice the state controlled religion through the Diyanet rather than strictly separating them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Kemalist laicism replaced religious law with secular codes and removed Islam's legal role.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A state-founding republican tradition treats justice and defence as state functions; the constitution vests them in state organs.

military-superiority.rationale: The doctrine of peace abroad conflicts with arms-race language but Kemalism prizes a strong army; split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Article 88 defines Turk as a political term including all citizens, and Kemalist nationalism is civic not ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Kemalist populism explicitly rejects class conflict and collectivism in favour of national unity.

civilizational-union.rationale: Kemalism turned away from Ottoman and Islamic unity toward a Western-oriented national state.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ağaoğlu treated egoism as the problem of Eastern societies and prized mutual aid and altruism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Ağaoğlu saw individual and state with mutual obligations but also natural individual rights; the constitution lists natural rights first.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Kemalism is a modernizing project that sought industrial and Western progress.

restore-past-order.rationale: Kemalism broke with the Ottoman past and aimed at progress toward Western lifestyles.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Atatürk described his creed as based on science and avoided dogma, but the tradition also has six formal principles; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A modernizing, progress-oriented creed that aimed at Western-style development rejects a return to hunter-gatherer life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolishing the division of labour is a utopian-communist aim that a private-enterprise modernizing programme has no place for.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist principle opposed by a creed that rejected collectivism and class politics.

production-for-use.rationale: The liberal wing favoured private, profit-driven enterprise over the planned production-for-need that the statement describes.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Kemalist populism rejects class conflict, and the liberal wing champions private enterprise.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejects class rule and collectivism; Ağaoğlu rejected both fascism and communism for Turkey.

collective-farming.rationale: A private-enterprise, anti-collectivist tradition opposes collectivization.

taxation-theft.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed state-funded pensions, health and education, which require taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Article 68 says the only limits on liberty are those protecting others' rights and liberties.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Ağaoğlu stressed political voice and parties; exit as the main check is not part of the tradition.

state-as-business.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized lack of transparency and nepotism but thought the state had social obligations beyond business logic.

positive-liberty.rationale: His welfare-state turn paired liberty with public pensions, health and education.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Civic Turkishness, equality regardless of race and the Enlightenment orientation reject racial determinism.

organic-representation.rationale: The 1924 constitution made the Assembly sole representative of the nation, individually elected; Kemalism abolished corporate estates.

total-state.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected fascism and communism and defended individual freedom of thought against the state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Kemalism did aim at national revival from Ottoman decline, but without a decadence narrative of the radical-right sort; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Republican sovereignty rests on the nation and the Assembly under Articles 3 and 4, not on personal oaths between lords and followers.

bound-labor.rationale: Article 73 and 70 protect labour and ban forced servitude-style practices; incompatible with liberal rights.

universal-morality.rationale: Ağaoğlu drew on French Enlightenment and republican thought seeking secular sources of morality.

single-common-good.rationale: Populism stressed national unity, but liberals accept competing parties; split leaning pluralist.

revive-national-language.rationale: Turkish language reform purified rather than revived a dead language; no direct relevance.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of firms by workers and the public is not part of a private-enterprise programme that disliked statist control.

school-vouchers.rationale: Kemalism centralized state education and secular schooling; Ağaoğlu viewed education as a state-led priority.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Free Republican party tied political freedom of press and thought to freer private enterprise.

rule-by-example.rationale: The tradition relies on laws and institutions rather than rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The republic arose from the War of Independence and national sovereignty is central, in Atatürk's tradition.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kemalism claimed science and reason as its guide and fought clerical influence, though it left personal faith free.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Ağaoğlu's welfare ideas are described without reference to who qualifies, so restriction to citizens is neither affirmed nor denied.

class-collaboration.rationale: Populism rejects class conflict and stresses national solidarity across classes.

dominated-front.rationale: Kemalism sought a Western orientation rather than a bloc of dominated countries.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported equal economic and political rights for women, so legally distinct public roles for men and women contradict his view.

ban-interest.rationale: A private-enterprise liberal programme embraces credit and foreign capital.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 69 abolishes group privileges and Article 88 includes all citizens.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This Marxist account of the state conflicts with Kemalist populism, which denies class division and stresses national unity.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The civic definition includes all citizens as Turks, yet Kemalism pursued cultural unification; adherents split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Ağaoğlu spoke of women's backwardness and clerical power as problems but did not frame it as structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

reviewHistory.rationale: Ağaoğlu denounced CHP corruption, nepotism and abuse of power after 1926, which supports an agreeing answer for a liberal Kemalist.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported welfare provision, so a minimal state is rejected despite liberal leanings.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Discouraging marriage across racial lines contradicts equality before the law irrespective of race and the civic definition of Turk.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Article 69 declares all Turks equal before the law and abolishes privileges.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate about socialism that Kemalism, which rejected class politics, never joined.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Kemalism replaced religious law with a single secular civil code, adopted from Switzerland.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article 75 says no one may be molested for religion or philosophic convictions.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Laicism centralized education under state control, ending madrasa instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist thesis about the socialist state is opposed to the tradition's rejection of class politics.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Article 3 says sovereignty belongs without restriction to the nation.

trade-surplus.rationale: A liberal programme welcomes open trade and foreign capital rather than mercantilism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian axiom that Kemalism, a state-building republican creed, does not endorse, though it shares Article 68's harm limit.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Economic competition is welcome but a struggle between peoples is not; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The founders required the Free Party to pledge to republicanism and secularism; the tradition defends the regime against its enemies.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican vocabulary appears in the tradition, but the sources do not articulate freedom as non-domination, so neutral.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist vanguard party is incompatible with liberal Kemalism, which sought multi-party democracy and rejected class politics.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Kemalism limited class organizing, but liberals protect association; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Filling offices by lottery conflicts with the elected Assembly model of the 1924 constitution and with Ağaoğlu's meritocratic emphasis.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kemalist history includes emergency rule, while the liberal strand defends legal rights, so adherents are split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A liberal economy opposes price controls in principle, but emergency measures were accepted in practice, so adherents split.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Free Republican Party promised freedom of the press and of thought, which contradicts party control of media.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Capping representatives' pay at a worker's wage is not a Kemalist or liberal position in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Article 3 says sovereignty belongs without restriction to the nation, which argues against pooling it in a supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The sources do not record a stance on who commands the armed forces, so adherents' views are unrecorded.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church organisation is irrelevant to Islam in Turkey, where the state controls religion through the Diyanet, so it is rejected as inapplicable.

clerical-rule.rationale: Laicism is aimed at breaking the dominance of the traditional religious establishment.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Kemalist nationalism rooted in a war of independence contradicts the call for workers to work for their own government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Article 77 prohibits prior censorship of the press and the party promised freedom of thought, which cuts against moral censorship of art.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Abolishing renting contradicts the property rights listed in the 1924 constitution and the party's liberal economy.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Modernizing urban reform; Kemalism favoured peasant education but not agrarian romanticism.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Ağaoğlu prized education and meritocracy, so claiming that educated people are out of touch cuts against his outlook.

death-penalty.rationale: Turkey retained capital punishment for decades while liberals dissent, and the sources do not record a view, so adherents split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A creed founded on science and reason and secular state education rejects teaching creationism in public schools.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Article 88 defines Turk as a political term covering all citizens, which favours a civic over descent-based approach.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Uniform secular law is a Kemalist principle, so exempting religious minorities from general laws is rejected.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Freedom of thought and individual liberty point to tolerance of nonconformity.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Atatürk's era valued economic independence but liberals favoured foreign capital.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Ağaoğlu opposed authoritarian hardening, though liberties were to have an educative role.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 74 allows expropriation for public interest but property is a natural right.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Laicism meant the state centralizing religious institutions, abolishing the caliphate and Sufi orders and creating the Diyanet.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not record a stance on a non-partisan head of state, so adherents' view is unrecorded.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A unitary state does not allow a region to join while keeping its own system, so this is rejected.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The republic replaced the sacral monarchy and caliphate, so regarding the head of state as sacred is rejected.

character-from-environment.rationale: Ağaoğlu emphasized education, upbringing and social context in his reform thinking.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Article 68 and constitutional rule limit rulers by law, which contradicts a ruler above the law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The republic uses a single sovereign Assembly representing the whole nation rather than mixing few and many, so this is rejected.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This doctrine about class struggle under socialism is rejected by a creed that denies class conflict.

land-redistribution.rationale: The constitution protects property as a natural right and the party favoured private enterprise, so seizing estates is rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Article 75 says no one may be molested on account of religion, sect or philosophic convictions, so punishing apostasy is rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: Kemalist reforms discouraged religious dress and promoted women's emancipation, so legally requiring cover is rejected.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Kemalism did not adopt Marxist historical materialism, preferring national unity and reform from above.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Free Republican programme called for an end to monopolies, supporting prohibition of cartels.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The party's openness to foreign capital and trade rejects an autarkic imperial economic bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: A private-enterprise programme relies on material incentives, so replacing them with moral incentives is rejected.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Article 69 abolished privileges of groups, classes and families, and Ağaoğlu favoured meritocracy.

patriotic-education.rationale: Kemalism centralized state education to create a national citizenry loyal to the republic, and Ağaoğlu backed Turkism and education reform as central tasks.

delink-world-market.rationale: The liberal wing wanted more tolerance for foreign capital and closer ties with the League of Nations, so economic delinking is contrary to its programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist thesis about class; Kemalist populism denies class division, so an adherent would not endorse it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Republicanism replaced the Ottoman monarchy with elected officials, so rulers are chosen by election among the national community.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1924 constitution makes the Grand National Assembly the sole lawful representative of the nation and says it exercises the legislative power directly (Articles 4-6), with no monarch above it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Ağaoğlu opposed inherited privilege yet stressed mutual obligations between individual and state, so a duty of the privileged to the less fortunate is neither clearly affirmed nor rejected.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ağaoğlu was a lifelong politically engaged reformer who wrote opposition programmes and reports to Atatürk, so withdrawal from public affairs contradicts the creed.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim not found in Kemalist sources, whose modernizing project sought to spread education and culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: This Gramscian thesis assumes a ruling class, which Kemalist populism denies in favour of national unity.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory conflicts with a programme that sought foreign capital and integration with the wider economy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Article 88 counts all citizens as Turks, but the early republic favoured the Muslim majority in practice, so adherents may split.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate internal to communist movements, with no connection to Kemalism; neutral by default.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The party welcomed foreign capital yet the republic stressed national independence, so adherents can lean either way.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The constitution treats all citizens as equally Turks under Article 88 and abolishes group privilege, leaving no basis for descent-based political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected fascism as a model for Turkey, but the republic's founding values are republican and national, not anti-fascist as such.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Kemalism aimed to move Turkey toward Western lifestyles and law, adopting European codes and institutions, so it denies that they suit only one civilization.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army saw itself as guardian of Kemalist principles, but liberal Kemalists criticized authoritarianism, so adherents split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Ağaoğlu stressed meritocracy over inherited privilege, which favours merit-based recruitment to public posts.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The Free Republican programme was more tolerant toward foreign capital than the CHP, so blocking takeovers cuts against it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Under the 1924 constitution the Assembly represents the nation as a whole rather than as binding delegates of constituents.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

land-use-tenure.rationale: The constitution lists property among natural rights, so community or national ownership of land with individuals only holding use rights is contrary to it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament was made the sole representative of the nation, and Ağaoğlu criticized parliamentary opacity, so parliamentary budget control is consistent.

single-official-language.rationale: Article 2 of the 1924 constitution makes Turkish the official language, and Kemalist nationalism stressed one common Turkish language and culture.

job-guarantee.rationale: Having the state guarantee jobs is an etatist measure of the kind the liberal wing opposed in favour of private enterprise.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A republic built on constitutional law and the rule of law expects obedience to legitimate laws.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Civil marriage under the secular civil code was a core Kemalist reform replacing religious marriage, so abolishing legal marriage is contrary to it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Ağaoğlu criticized the lack of transparency and parliamentary opacity under CHP rule.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty belongs to the nation, yet the Free Republican Party wanted closer League of Nations ties, so adherents split.

religious-nation.rationale: Article 88 says the name Turk as a political term includes all citizens, defining the nation by citizenship rather than shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The republic was founded by resisting foreign domination and claims unrestricted national sovereignty, so ritual deference is rejected.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: The question presupposes common ownership of production, which the party rejected, but personal belongings are uncontroversial; no clear position.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

defeat-communism.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected communism as a model, but the sources don't describe an active crusade to defeat it, and Atatürk's Turkey coexisted with the USSR.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ağaoğlu argued for equal economic and political rights for women within the existing order rather than for transforming the economy.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing cooperative communities are an anarchist-style model far from a private-enterprise republican programme.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ağaoğlu rejected communism and fascism but favoured a market economy with welfare, so he did not seek a third system.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The republic renounced irredentism, but nothing is said about the strength of historical claims in general.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The party was created to give multi-party democracy a platform, and Ağaoğlu criticized the abuse of power under one-party rule.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Article 75 says no one may be molested for religion or philosophic convictions, and a secular state does not enforce religious offence.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Laicism removes religious law from public duty, though Ottoman-era resistance used religious language.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Laicism makes rulers answerable to secular law, so declaring rulers illegitimate for not following religious law is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Ağaoğlu valued democracy but held that liberties should have an educative function, so wide direct participation is not clearly endorsed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Kemalist populism claimed to transcend classes, but liberal Kemalists place themselves in a centre-right opposition tradition, so adherents split.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept that is alien to a creed rejecting class conflict.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Article 3 says sovereignty belongs without restriction to the nation, not to God.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ağaoğlu combined a more liberal economy with pensions, health and education, a market-with-welfare position.

rich-first.rationale: The party favoured private enterprise and foreign capital, which tolerates uneven growth, but nothing says so explicitly.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Republicanism abolished hereditary rule and Ağaoğlu opposed inherited privilege.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A private-enterprise programme tolerant of foreign capital relies on ordinary interest-bearing credit.

property-franchise.rationale: Article 69 makes all Turks equal before the law, and the republic extended the vote rather than restricting it by wealth.

racial-franchise.rationale: Article 69 makes all Turks equal before the law, and Article 88 includes every citizen.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The secular civil code replaced religious marriage law, removing religious restrictions.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Laicism meant state neutrality and control of religion, and Atatürk kept private belief free, so promoting atheism is rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Ağaoğlu backed state pensions and social benefits, not charity as the main answer.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported gender equality and women's independence, and the secular civil code removed male legal authority.

rent-control.rationale: Price and rent caps are statist interventions the liberal wing opposed in favour of private enterprise.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: National sovereignty argues against foreign bases while Western alignment argues for them; adherents split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Ağaoğlu valued merit over inherited privilege but defended a private-enterprise order, so adherents split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Laicism and a science-and-reason basis reject framing politics as a spiritual struggle.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A Marxist test of socialism that does not apply to a creed rejecting class politics.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1924 constitution set up a single assembly, and sources don't record the liberal strand's view.

municipal-property.rationale: Local community ownership of the means of production contradicts a private-enterprise programme.

confederal-coordination.rationale: A confederation of self-governing towns contradicts the unitary republic.

person-over-state.rationale: Ağaoğlu presented the individual and the state as having mutual obligations and defended individual natural rights, though he balanced this with communitarian ideas.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: In a unitary republic, regional powers rest on national legislation and can be changed by it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Equality before the law and civic citizenship reject racial political blocs.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Article 88 defines Turk politically as all citizens, though Kemalism also stressed a common language and culture.

communal-electorates.rationale: The unitary civic nation with equal citizens rejects separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Sèvres-syndrome suspicion is common in Kemalist nationalism, but the liberal strand is more open to the West, so adherents split.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: Ağaoğlu valued women's educated role as mothers but also equal rights, so adherents split on whether women bring distinct values.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

arms-reduction.rationale: The party sought closer ties with the League of Nations, but arms reduction is not described in sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The republic itself is the state built by the Kemalist revolution, so smashing it is rejected.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Ağaoğlu drew on French Enlightenment and republican thought and on natural rights, which presuppose a shared human nature.

workers-own-party.rationale: Kemalist populism rejects class politics and favours national unity in a single party framework.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported equal economic and political rights for women, and the secular civil code gave women equal inheritance rights.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Kemalist populism shifted legitimacy away from tribal leaders to citizens, so chiefs in lawmaking are rejected.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Article 75 protects each sect but the state in practice controlled religion through the Diyanet and favoured one interpretation, so adherents split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The party sought free multi-party elections, but liberals also value liberties, so adherents split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The party promised freedom of press and thought, so state shutdown of communications is contrary to it.

women-suffrage.rationale: Ağaoğlu supported equal economic and political rights for women, the reasoning being that they must take part in public life.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Ağaoğlu named the backwardness of women and the power of clerics as the two main problems in the Muslim world.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The party sought closer ties with the League of Nations, but tribunals for leaders are not mentioned.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The liberal wing opposed statist planning and rejected communism as a model for Turkey.

indirect-election.rationale: The 1924 constitution had parliament elect the president, but sources don't record a stance on tiered election.

national-church-status.rationale: Laicism removed Islam's special legal status, though the state kept control of religion through the Diyanet.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The unitary republic with all citizens as Turks leaves no room for territorial autonomy.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The strand stresses individual liberties and constitutional guarantees, as in the 1924 constitution, which do not allow killing without trial.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The strand criticized the CHP's one-party authoritarianism and its 1930 party stood for multi-party democracy.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Secular republicanism and laicism are core to Kemalism and to this strand, so religion is not a basis for parties.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Ağaoğlu argued for women's equal rights and secular morality, which supports a wife's right to end a marriage.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The Free Republican Party was founded to end one-party rule with multi-party competition and private enterprise, so party-led socialism contradicts it.

missingStatements.text: A country's alphabet and writing system may be changed by law to modernize it.
missingStatements.rationale: Ağaoğlu pushed alphabet reform and cultural modernization, a defining Kemalist reform no current statement captures.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow: a one-off Kemalist reform that other ideologies rarely take a side on.

notes: Sources on this strand are thin and partly contested: Wikipedia's Liberal Kemalism article flags unsourced claims, and scholars note Ağaoğlu's liberalism was communitarian and reliant on state-led change. Strict etatist Kemalists would answer economic and state-power statements differently.
